f209.summary: During his embassy to Rome for Henri IV's absolution, Nevers writes to Pisany that people were dissuading the King from seeking the Pope's absolution, that he (Nevers) argued there was no need for him to go without it, and that if there is no will to satisfy the Pope one should not go at all.

f168.summary: Written the day after Possevino's message at Poschiavo: the Duke of Nevers will not be received as ambassador for several reasons; Nevers reports what he was told and his intention to advance and do as he was written, with Cardinal Gondi and the Duke of Mantua named. Read in long stretches; several passages remain garbled by the copyist's figures.

system: Nevers cipher no. 46: a two-digit alphabet with homophones and nulls, and barred, plain and double-dotted figure series for words and names.
